I farm only 4.5 mu, so every bag of fertilizer costs me real money. I do not make big changes unless I see they work nearby. For my wheat-maize land, I will mostly follow what has worked for me in the last few years and what other people around me are doing. Wheat cannot be short of base fertilizer, or the seedlings stay weak through winter, so I will put enough before sowing and then topdress once when it starts growing strongly in spring. Maize is the same idea: if fertilizer is too light, the ears come out small, and that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra on one more bag. I have well water, so I will use irrigation at the key times instead of gambling on rain. On my small area, I do not need to chase fancy methods. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I have seen those do better than old seed when the field is managed properly. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it is easier on my small plot in the wheat-maize rotation and costs less labor than deep ploughing every season. I will keep pesticide use to what is commonly done here: not too many sprays, but I will not skip them if disease, aphids, or armyworm show up.
